      id: 5a137618-2f46-4a38-b74a-8e3d878055aa

      the document's own date: 2025-08-20 (issued)
      the date that matters: 2025-08-20 (last_entry)
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is a maintenance service record documenting annual inspection and servicing of 14 portable fire extinguishers at the Portland facility, performed by a licensed technician in accordance with NFPA 10 (2022). All units passed inspection and are ready for use; the company must conduct monthly visual inspections of each unit and schedule the next annual maintenance by August 20, 2026, with special attention to units W-3 and L-1 which require six-year internal maintenance before November 2026.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT: nothing
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT OBLIGES THEM TO KEEP DOING (4), read out of the document itself:
        · NFPA 10, Section 7.2 — Monthly visual inspection of all fire extinguishers
            the evidence you would expect to see: Monthly inspection tags or records on each extinguisher documenting date, inspector name, and condition checks
        · NFPA 10, Section 7.3 and Oregon OAR 437-002-0187(2) — Annual maintenance by certified technician
            the evidence you would expect to see: Current maintenance certificate with technician license, date, and results for each unit
        · NFPA 10, Section 7.3.6 — Six-year internal maintenance for W-3 and L-1
            the evidence you would expect to see: Maintenance certificate documenting internal examination, disassembly, inspection, and refilling before November 2026
        · NFPA 10, Chapter 8 — Hydrostatic testing at prescribed intervals
            the evidence you would expect to see: Hydrostatic test records showing test date, pressure results, and technician credentials for each unit when interval arrives
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (2):
        · Annual maintenance renewal for all units — 2026-08-20 (recurring)
        · Six-year internal maintenance for units W-3 and L-1 — 2026-11-30
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (4) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · Hydrostatic test records — Various units will require hydrostatic testing at 12-year intervals (dry chemical and CO2 types per manufacture date); no records of completed tests are listed.
        · Monthly visual inspection log for period August 2025 to September 2026 — NFPA 10, Section 7.2 and Oregon regulations require monthly visual inspections with records kept on unit tags; a complete set would show compliance.
        · Six-year internal maintenance certificate for units W-3 and L-1 — These units reach their six-year interval in 2026 and require internal examination before November 2026; no certificate for this work appears in the company records.
        · Updated annual maintenance certificate (2026) — The previous certificate is dated August 2025; renewal was due August 20, 2026 and the current date is September 29, 2026, indicating overdue maintenance.

  --- Monthly EHS Self-Check
      id: 88f0951e-ceaa-4cf7-95de-d5d5937aa66d
      file: 13-company-self-check.docx
      kind: program · status: not_judged · shown as: on_file
      the document's own date: none stated (unknown)
      the date that matters: none
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is a monthly self-inspection checklist designed to track compliance with workplace safety, air quality, fire safety, and chemical handling standards. The company completes this form to verify that key controls are in place each month — air permit posted and valid, scrubber pressure-drop readings logged within operating ranges, detector-tube checks performed, equipment inspections done, fire extinguishers current, exits clear, eyewash and safety showers functional, and safety data sheets available. Any item marked 'N' must be reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT (8) — these are already findings; carry them, do not re-find them:
        · No document date or completion record visible
            The template shows blanks for Month, Completed by, and Supervisor with no dates or initials filled in. Without a completed instance of this form, it is not possible to verify whether the company is performing these checks or how recent the most recent check was.
            what it needs: Obtain a completed monthly self-check form showing the month reviewed, the date of supervisor review, the employee who completed it, and the results (Y/N and initials) for each line item. Confirm the company fills this out every month.
            the rule: OSHA General Duty Clause (OSH Act Section 5(a)(1)); OAR 340-216-8010 et seq. (Oregon air permit posting and availability requirements)
        · No procedure for tracking or escalating failures  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            The form states 'Items marked N are reported to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month' but does not specify what happens next — no procedure for investigation, root cause, corrective action, documentation, or verification that issues are fixed before the next month.
            what it needs: Establish a written procedure defining: (1) what constitutes an 'N' result, (2) who investigates, (3) required corrective actions by category, (4) documentation requirements, (5) verification that fixes are in place before the next check, (6) escalation criteria for repeated failures or safety risks.
            the rule: OSHA General Duty Clause; 29 CFR 1910.22 (general safety requirements); Oregon DEQ permit conditions typically require prompt correction of deficiencies
        · Missing scope for Line 3 — C-1 detector-tube check frequency and method  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 3 calls for 'Weekly C-1 detector-tube checks done and recorded every week this month' but the checklist does not specify what constitutes a valid check (e.g., testing method, recording format, pass/fail criteria, action if outlet exceeds threshold).
            what it needs: Add to the procedure or attach a reference document: the standard or protocol for C-1 outlet detector-tube testing, the acceptable range or pass criterion, the required log format, and what corrective action is required if the check shows a failure.
            the rule: Oregon air permit conditions for scrubber outlet monitoring (likely specified in Permit 26-2841-ST-01 or its attachments); ANSI/ASABE standard or equivalent
        · Missing acceptance range for Line 2 — scrubber pressure-drop readings
            Line 2 specifies 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0' but does not clarify the units (inches water column, bar, kPa, etc.) or reference the source permit condition that sets this range.
            what it needs: Amend Line 2 to state the units of measurement (e.g., 'readings between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column') and add a reference to the permit condition or design document that establishes this range.
            the rule: Oregon air permit conditions for scrubber operations; company's own Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log document already exists
        · No definition of defect follow-up documentation for Line 4  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 4 requires 'any defect followed up' but does not specify what follow-up means — repair timelines, work orders, log entries, supervisor approval, or sign-off required.
            what it needs: Add to the procedure or manual: define 'follow-up' to include (1) creation of work order or incident report, (2) severity/urgency category, (3) repair deadline (e.g., before next use, within 24 hours, within one week), (4) required documentation (photos, maintenance log entry, mechanic's sign-off), and (5) verification that defect was corrected before the truck next runs.
            the rule: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178 (powered industrial truck operation and maintenance); company's own PIT Pre-Shift Inspection Log already documents daily checks
        · Fire extinguisher tag protocol not specified  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 5 states fire extinguishers must be 'tagged within the last 12 months; monthly visual check initialled on each tag' but does not specify who performs the monthly check (technician or any employee), where initials go, or what visual checks constitute pass/fail.
            what it needs: Add procedures for fire extinguisher maintenance: (1) annual professional inspection/recharge must be performed by a certified service company; (2) monthly visual walk-through: check for damage, blockage, pressure gauge in green zone; (3) log and initial a tag on the extinguisher or maintain a separate log; (4) any defect triggers immediate service or replacement. Reference NFPA 10 or equivalent.
            the rule: NFPA 10 (Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157 (general requirements for all portable fire extinguishers)
        · Eyewash and safety shower flush protocol incomplete  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 7 calls for 'Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged' but does not specify duration of flush, acceptance criteria, or where logs are kept.
            what it needs: Add to the procedure: (1) flushing frequency (at minimum weekly; some standards require daily or when in use); (2) flush duration (typically 1–3 minutes to clear lines); (3) visual inspection for water flow, clarity, and nozzle function; (4) log entry must include date, time, location, flush duration, any defects noted, and initials; (5) any malfunction must trigger repair/replacement before next work day.
            the rule: ANSI Z535.4 (labeling and marking of hazardous substances); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151 (eye and face protection); many states and facilities follow ANSI Z535.1 or local code for emergency equipment inspection
        · SDS binder update protocol undefined  [worked out from the document, not stated in it]
            Line 8 requires 'Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated' but does not define who updates the index, how indexing is organized, or how obsolete SDSs are removed.
            what it needs: Add to the SDS management procedure: (1) designate responsible person(s); (2) require SDS to be obtained and added to binder within X days of receipt (commonly within 5–10 days); (3) organize by product name, CAS number, or hazard category with consistent labeling; (4) maintain an index or log with product name, receipt date, SDS version date, and location in binder; (5) remove and archive obsolete SDSs (keep for X years per record retention policy); (6) verify accessibility during inspections; (7) train all employees on binder location and use.
            the rule: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(g) (Hazard Communication Standard, SDS requirements)
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (1):
        · Items marked N reported to Plant Manager — no date stated (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (7) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · Completed monthly forms for prior months — To verify the company is actually conducting these checks monthly and responding to failures, a history of completed forms is essential. Without them, the template is a procedure document only, not evidence of compliance.
        · Escalation or investigation log for 'N' results — The checklist states failures go to the Plant Manager by the 5th of the following month, but no log of those reports, investigations, or remediation actions was provided. This is critical evidence that problems are addressed.
        · Exit route and emergency egress audit or floor plan — Line 6 checks that exits and aisles are clear and signs are lit, but no floor plan, exit signage documentation, or periodic egress audit procedure is provided.
        · Fire extinguisher maintenance contract or service record — Line 5 requires annual professional tagging and monthly checks. The company should hold a service contract and annual maintenance records, which are missing from the submission.
        · Powered Industrial Truck operator training and evaluation records — The company has a 'Powered Industrial Truck Operator Training and Evaluation Record' in its document list, but how that links to the pre-shift inspection protocol on Line 4 is not shown.
        · Scrubber maintenance and testing SOP — Line 2 and 3 reference specific monitoring ranges and detector-tube checks, but the actual procedure, acceptance criteria, and corrective-action thresholds are not attached or incorporated.
        · SDS master list or binder with current index — Line 8 requires an updated SDS binder and index. The template does not show how many chemicals are in inventory or what the current index looks like.
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT SAYS, proposed by the reading, not confirmed by anyone (1):
        · inspection checklist sections: 8 line items covering air permit, scrubber monitoring, detector-tube checks, forklift inspections, fire extinguisher maintenance, exit routes, eyewash/safety showers, and safety data sheets
            it says: "8 check items numbered 1–8"
            where: table rows

      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (3):

documents.title: OSHA Form 300A Summary of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses for Year 2025
documents.summary: This is OSHA Form 300A, the annual summary of recordable work-related injuries and illnesses for calendar year 2025. The form is required to be completed by employers with 10 or more employees and must be posted in a visible workplace location from February 1 through April 30 of the following year. The form documents that Cascade Specialty Chemicals had 3 recordable cases in 2025 (1 case with days away from work, 2 other recordable cases), with 6 total days away from work and no fatalities.

findings.title: Eyewash and safety shower flushing protocol (Line 7 of monthly self-check)
findings.locator: Line 7: 'Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged'
findings.quote: Line 7 calls for 'Eyewash stations and safety showers flushed this week and logged' but does not specify duration of flush, acceptance criteria, or where logs are kept.
findings.what_to_do: Add to the procedure: (1) flushing frequency (at minimum weekly; some standards require daily or when in use); (2) flush duration (typically 1–3 minutes to clear lines); (3) visual inspection for water flow, clarity, and nozzle function; (4) log entry must include date, time, location, flush duration, any defects noted, and initials; (5) any malfunction must trigger repair/replacement before next work day

findings.title: Safety Data Sheet management and binder update protocol (Line 8 of monthly self-check)
findings.locator: Line 8: 'Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated'
findings.quote: Line 8 requires 'Safety data sheets on hand for every chemical received this month; binder index updated' but does not define who updates the index, how indexing is organized, or how obsolete SDSs are removed.
findings.what_to_do: Add to the SDS management procedure: (1) designate responsible person(s); (2) require SDS to be obtained and added to binder within X days of receipt (commonly within 5–10 days); (3) organize by product name, CAS number, or hazard category with consistent labeling; (4) maintain an index or log with product name, receipt date, SDS version date, and location in binder; (5) remove and archive obsolete SDSs (keep for X years per record retention policy); (6) verify accessibility during inspections; (7) train all employees on binder location and use

findings.title: OSHA Form 300A posting in workplace
findings.what_to_do: Verify that the form is or was posted in a conspicuous location where employee notices are customarily displayed from 2026-02-01 through 2026-04-30; if not yet posted, post immediately until April 30

findings.what_to_do: File and retain the Form 300A and underlying OSHA Form 300 Log through 2030-12-31 (five years following end of calendar year covered); verify supporting Form 301 incident reports are retained for each of the 3 recordable cases

expected_not_seen.title: Documentation of posting location and dates for OSHA Form 300A
expected_not_seen.why: Similar employers typically document where the form was posted and on what dates to verify compliance with the February 1 through April 30 posting window

expected_not_seen.title: OSHA Form 300 Log (detailed injury and illness log)
expected_not_seen.why: The Form 300A is a summary; the underlying Form 300 Log with individual case details must also be retained for five years and should be on file

expected_not_seen.title: OSHA Form 301 Incident Reports
expected_not_seen.why: Each of the 3 recordable cases documented on the Form 300A should have a corresponding Form 301 with detailed incident information

expected_not_seen.title: Fire extinguisher maintenance contract or service records from a licensed vendor
expected_not_seen.why: Companies with annual fire extinguisher maintenance requirements typically retain a service contract and maintain copies of annual maintenance certificates from a certified vendor

expected_not_seen.title: Escalation or investigation log for monthly self-check failures
expected_not_seen.why: When 'N' results are reported to the Plant Manager, similar companies document the investigation, root cause, corrective actions taken, and verification of fixes

expected_not_seen.title: Scrubber maintenance and testing Standard Operating Procedure
expected_not_seen.why: The monthly self-check references specific scrubber monitoring ranges and detector-tube checks; companies typically maintain an SOP detailing the testing method, acceptance criteria, and corrective-action thresholds

expected_not_seen.title: Master SDS list or binder with current index
expected_not_seen.why: Companies holding SDSs for multiple chemicals typically maintain a master list or organized binder with an index showing product name, receipt date, SDS version date, and location

expected_not_seen.title: Exit route and emergency egress audit or floor plan
expected_not_seen.why: The monthly self-check requires verification that exits and aisles are clear and signs are lit; companies typically maintain a floor plan, exit signage documentation, or a periodic egress audit procedure
